one_line: Court poet Rajashekhara and his learned wife Avantisundari at Mahendrapala I’s Kannauj, shaping Sanskrit literary theory and education.

appearance.age_look: Rajashekhara appears as a lithe man in his mid-30s; Avantisundari as a poised woman in her early 30s, both with dignified, scholarly bearing.
appearance.face: Rajashekhara has an oval face, medium-brown North Indian complexion, straight nose, neatly groomed short beard and mustache, and keen, thoughtful large anime eyes with a calm half-smile; Avantisundari has a heart-shaped face, similar medium-brown complexion, expressive almond eyes, straight nose, and a serene, intelligent default expression showing gentle curiosity.
appearance.hair: Rajashekhara’s black hair is parted in the middle and drawn into a tidy high knot at the back crown, secured with a simple gold pin and leaving a smooth front; Avantisundari’s long black hair is center-parted, oiled and braided, coiled into a low bun at the nape, framed by a narrow gold headband and a soft saffron veil draped from the back of her head over her shoulders.
appearance.costume: Rajashekhara wears a finely draped, knee-length cream-colored cotton uttariya (upper cloth) over a fitted, long-sleeved pale saffron angarkha-style tunic tied at the side, with a dark maroon silk-bordered dhoti wrapped in the northern style to the ankles, simple brown leather sandals, a thin gold necklace with a small round pendant, narrow gold bangles on one wrist, and a waist cord from which hangs a small palm-leaf manuscript case; Avantisundari wears a full-length deep indigo sari in 9th-century north Indian style, pleats front and hem to the ankles, with a rich maroon and gold woven border, wrapped over a modest short-sleeved cream blouse and drawn over her left shoulder, plus a light saffron veil falling from her headband; she is adorned with small gold stud earrings, a delicate gold nose-ring on the left side, a simple gold mangalsutra-style necklace, a few thin gold bangles on each wrist, and comfortable brown sandals, her garments in plain weaves with subtle stripe patterns at the borders only.
appearance.signature: Rajashekhara carries a polished palm-leaf manuscript wrapped in a dark maroon cloth and a slender stylus tucked into his waist cord, while Avantisundari carries a small, rectangular wooden writing board with a palm-leaf strip and stylus resting upon it.

ref_desc: Rajashekhara is a medium-brown, bearded man with a high-knot black hairstyle, cream uttariya, pale saffron tunic, maroon-bordered dhoti and manuscript bundle, beside Avantisundari, a medium-brown woman with braided bun, indigo sari with maroon-gold border, saffron veil and wooden writing board, in cream, indigo, maroon, saffron and gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character pair of Rajashekhara and Avantisundari from 9th-century Kannauj court culture, standing side by side as scholarly partners. Rajashekhara is a lithe man in his mid-30s with a medium-brown North Indian complexion, oval face, neat short beard and mustache, and large thoughtful eyes, his black hair parted and tied into a tidy high knot at the back crown secured with a simple gold pin. He wears a finely draped cream cotton uttariya over a fitted, long-sleeved pale saffron angarkha-style tunic tied at the side, and a dark maroon silk-bordered dhoti wrapped to the ankles, with simple brown leather sandals, a thin gold necklace with a small round pendant, narrow gold bangles on one wrist, and a waist cord holding a small palm-leaf manuscript case. His signature prop is a polished palm-leaf manuscript wrapped in dark maroon cloth held in one hand, with a slender stylus tucked into his waist cord. Beside him, Avantisundari is a poised woman in her early 30s with a heart-shaped face, medium-brown complexion, serene intelligent expression and large anime almond eyes, her long black hair center-parted, braided and coiled into a low bun at the nape, framed by a narrow gold headband and a soft saffron veil draped from the back of her head over her shoulders. She wears a full-length deep indigo sari in 9th-century north Indian style with rich maroon and gold woven border, modestly covering a short-sleeved cream blouse, pleats in front and hem to the ankles, and comfortable brown sandals; the sari and blouse are plain-weave with subtle stripes only at the borders. Her jewelry includes small gold stud earrings, a delicate gold nose-ring on the left, a simple gold necklace, and a few thin gold bangles on each wrist. Her signature prop is a small rectangular wooden writing board held in her hands, with a palm-leaf strip and stylus resting on it. Use a harmonious palette of cream, deep indigo, maroon, saffron and gold, and clearly show their hair, faces, layered garments, modest coverage, sandals and scholarly tools in a clean model-sheet style that can be redrawn consistently.
